**The tenth**: that he be of little speech, low of voice, of little jest, of little oath-taking by God (even truthfully). Let no lie ever run upon his tongue at all; let him not enter the assemblies of frivolity; let him not rejoice in what the populace rejoices in of the world's pleasures — out of humility and lowering, not out of self-elevation and self-protection — as the Friend said: "I have not sat in the council of mockers, and I have rejoiced; from the face of Your hand I have sat alone, for You have filled me with indignation" (Jeremiah 15:17).

He said: As for the marks by which humility is verified in the humble man when they appear upon him — they are in five occurrences.

**The first**: at the time of the severity of his anger against one who has offended him by speech or deed. If he has ruled his caprice and pardoned after his capacity to take requital, in humility and lowering — that points to the soundness of his humility.

**The second**: when a misfortune in his wealth or a calamity in his household befalls him. If he prefers patience over alarm, in surrender to God's decree and contentment with His judgment — that points to the goodness of his humility and his abasement before God (mighty and exalted) — as Scripture said of Aaron (peace be upon him) at his trial in Nadab and Abihu: "And Aaron was silent" (Leviticus 10:3); and He said: "Be silent for the Lord and writhe before Him" (Psalms 37:7); and He said: "Therefore the prudent at that time shall be silent" (Amos 5:13).
